summary: Resolve and refresh connector OAuth access tokens at the host runtime boundary with PostgreSQL-serialized immutable secret rotation.

impacts.evidence: Refresh locks, secret reads and rotations are keyed by explicit organization/workspace scope plus opaque reference.
OAuth material remains encrypted and excluded from normal records, events, audit and API views.
Existing OAuth and account-health operations are reused without schema or operation changes.
No event names or payloads change and token material remains prohibited from events.
SDK v1 signatures stay frozen; OAuth primary-secret behavior is corrected to project only access-token bytes.
Existing immutable secret versions and transaction advisory locks require no schema migration.
Refresh/client secrets stay host-only; fixed manifest egress is TLS, DNS-pinned, public-address and redirect-deny.
Credential maintenance does not broaden connector capabilities or bypass business approval policy.
Stable opaque identity and immutable secret version lineage record each successful rotation without secret-bearing audit payloads.
A distributed advisory lock and post-lock reread prevent duplicate use of rotating refresh tokens.
Only exact manifest token endpoint egress is added; webhook behavior is unchanged.
Bounded refresh-failed and reauthorization-required health reasons distinguish remediation paths without raw errors.
Secret versions remain compatible, but rolling back runtime code reintroduces bundle projection and must not accompany OAuth connector admission.
Deterministic tests cover freshness, concurrent single refresh, rotation, reauthorization, client credentials and adapter projection.
